2608.25261.title: Hierarchical MoE for Multi-Modal ILD Diagnosis
2608.25261.paper_summary: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models combine specialized predictors under learned routing, offering a principled mechanism for leveraging heterogeneity in medical data. We present a hierarchical multimodal MoE for interstitial lung disease (ILD) classification that integrates a frozen, pre-trained imaging expert with structured electronic health records (EHR) via two-stage gating. A modality-level gate assigns patient-specific weights to imaging and EHR predictions, while a sub-gating module decomposes the EHR branch into clinically defined feature groups with learned, group-specific contributions. This design preserves stable imaging representations while enabling input-dependent clinical weighting and explicit EHR specialization. Under strict patient-level cross-validation, the model achieved the highest mean AUC among the evaluated methods (0.8750 +- 0.0443), compared with 0.8646 for imaging-only REN and 0.7685 for SwinUNETR. The framework extends interpretability across anatomical regions, imaging--EHR utilization, and clinically defined EHR feature groups.
2608.25261.paper_summary_zh: 混合專家（MoE）模型在學習路由下結合了專門的預測器，提供了一種利用醫療數據異質性的原則性機制。我們提出了一種層次化的多模態 MoE，用於間質性肺病（ILD）分類，該模型通過兩階段閘控將凍結的預訓練影像專家與結構化電子健康紀錄（EHR）整合在一起。模態級閘控為影像和 EHR 預測分配特定於患者的權重，而子閘控模塊則將 EHR 分支分解為臨床定義的特徵組，並具有學習到的特定於組的貢獻。這一設計保持了穩定的影像表示，同時使得輸入依賴的臨床加權和明確的 EHR 專業化成為可能。在嚴格的患者級交叉驗證下，該模型在評估的方法中達到了最高的平均 AUC（0.8750 ± 0.0443），相比之下，影像專用的 REN 為 0.8646，SwinUNETR 為 0.7685。該框架擴展了在解剖區域、影像—EHR 利用和臨床定義的 EHR 特徵組之間的可解釋性。
